extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, UIC staff, claimants and their representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing Boards of Referees and the appeal process under the Unemployment Insurance Act (composition, appointment, training, jurisdiction, filing, and related procedural rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Board of Referees
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board of referees is composed of a chairman and at least two members, divided evenly amongst two classes, 'employers or representatives of employers' and 'insured persons or representatives of insured persons'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairmen are appointed by the Governor in Council and other members are appointed by the UIC. The Board is constituted afresh for each appeal from panels of members (one panel for each class and a panel of chairmen). Once a decision is handed down the Board ceases to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tripartite principle / representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of employers and employees on the Board so contributors to the scheme may intervene directly in decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This legitimizes administrative action by associating representatives of the two sectors most directly concerned; the composition aims to synthesize individual interests into the public interest rather than reflect adversarial representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of Boards of referees must act impartially and consider the public interest as defined by Parliament after synthesizing the individual interests of both classes of contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is essential: a member 'must act impartially' and cannot be a representative or agent of any party. Impartiality is the sine qua non for chairmen; for representative members the requirement of impartiality is replaced by membership in the class they represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panels and non-permanence of Boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards are not permanent bodies with fixed members; they are constituted from panels (chairmen, employers' representatives, employees' representatives) established at the district level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels allow rotation/selection; exceptions exist for low-appeal districts and metropolitan pooling (e.g., Montreal and Vancouver).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment criteria for chairmen
rubrics_metrics.description: A UIC internal document lists requirements for chairmen, including: secondary education; availability; age under 70; residence in district; language ability; knowledge of labour conditions; prominence; intellectual capacity for legal work; capacity for judgment, analysis and synthesis; ability to write clearly and concisely; ability to direct the work of the Board; impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of these, impartiality is an absolute requirement; other criteria need only be largely satisfied. The Regional Office verifies requirements; Minister recommends candidates to Governor in Council; UIC may attempt accommodation if it finds a ministerial nominee unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment procedure for chairmen
rubrics_metrics.description: When a chairman vacancy arises the District Office notifies national HQ via the Regional Office; the Secretary notifies the Minister of Manpower and Immigration who recommends a candidate to the Governor in Council after consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional Office studies candidates for suitability, Secretary obtains opinion of the Unemployment Insurance Commissioners, and UIC concurrence is transmitted to the Minister signed by the Chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection/appointment of representative members
rubrics_metrics.description: For replacing or appointing a member, the Unemployment Insurance Commissioner requests nominations from organizations representative of employers or employees (e.g., CMA, CLC); Regional Office verifies suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suitable, the Commission appoints the member on its own authority. For representatives, the impartiality requirement is replaced by membership of the class to be represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure and termination of members vs chairmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are appointed for a stipulated period and may be terminated at any time by the Commission; chairmen have an indefinite mandate and terminating a chairman requires the intervention of the Minister and the Governor in Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation references: reg. 178(1) for members; sec. 91(2) discussed for chairmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial training for new referees (three-stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle new members receive a three-stage initial training: (1) meet senior District Office staff and receive documentation, (2) attend a Board session as an observer with documentation on appeals, (3) a day of instruction on main substantive provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation includes the Act, Regulations, Digest of Benefit Entitlement Principles, UIC Manual volumes, Umpires' collected decisions (CUB reports), a short manual, bulletins, and remuneration documentation. In practice some referees did not receive full training and relied on on-the-job learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing education for referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing education is provided via lectures once or twice a year by Regional Office officials and via periodic bulletins from the Entitlement Determination Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lectures cover procedure, difficult substantive questions, recent amendments, and specific problematic trends; bulletins describe developments in legislation, Umpires' caselaw and administrative practice. Frequency varies by region; many referees complain about insufficient time to digest documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration for Board sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 91(4) stipulates pay for members: for a session of more than four hours the chairman is entitled to $85 and other referees $65 each; for no more than four hours $50 for chairman and $40 for others; travel reimbursement up to $15 for referees living more than fifty miles from session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration and travel allowances are part of the practical organization and may affect availability and turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Board has a clerk (a UIC employee in senior clerical classification) whose duties include organizing sessions, compiling the roll of appeals, constituting the Board, convening members and appellants, compiling appeal statistics, documenting the Board and preparing the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The clerk may be consulted by the Board on technical points or asked to collect additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal and standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 94(1) gives both claimants and their employers the right to appeal to the Board of referees against any 'decision of the Commission'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants appeal decisions denying or withdrawing benefits; employers typically appeal decisions granting benefits where the Record of Employment indicated quit, labour dispute, misconduct, etc. Employer appeals are infrequent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects and extent of the Board's review powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may rescind or amend the initial decision and substitute its own judgment for that of the originator; absent legislative limitation the appeal is broad but circumscribed by rules inherent in the appeal logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two limiting rules: (1) the Board may pronounce only on questions before it and only settle questions inseparable from the appeal; (2) the Board may not go beyond the parties' claims or aggravate the claimant's position (e.g., cannot reopen issues previously settled in claimant's favour or impose harsher sanctions than the Agent II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction: matters within and excluded from Board authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction extends to all UIC decisions concerning a specific claim for benefit (disentitlements, disqualifications, penalties under sec. 47, determination of incapacity, denial of benefit, refusal to antedate a claim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded from review: actions that are not 'decisions' (e.g., mathematical calculation of overpayment), actions resulting from Commission's discretionary power (e.g., writing off overpayment), decisions outside Commission authority such as insurable employment (must be referred to Minister of National Revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic internal re‑examination when appeal filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an appeal triggers an automatic internal review: the Agent II must re-examine the file to determine whether facts alleged justify amending the initial decision; appeal proceeds only if the decision is upheld after re-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies cited: e.g., Quebec assistance group reported 29% of appeals withdrawn after re-examination; UIC study during a test week in 1973 found ~14% decisions amended and 29% abandoned after discussion, so ~43% of filed appeals did not reach the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effects of employer appeals and appeals against retroactive decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer-filed appeals do not result in withholding of benefit for period prior to Board decision; appeals against retroactive decisions resulting in overpayment must be brought to recoveries section which will suspend recovery actions pending Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves benefits to claimants and pauses debt recovery processes during appeal resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing the notice of appeal: timeline and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be filed within thirty days of the date on which the claimant or employer receives notification of the decision (sec. 94(1)); appeals may be filed by writing a letter to the UIC office where the decision was made (reg. 179) stating the grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dispute about date of receipt, UIC certification of mailing is evidence of receipt (sec. 120(2)). Extensions: Agent II may grant up to 30 days (UIC Manual sec. 442.1.5); Regional Office up to 120 days; extensions beyond that handled by Entitlement Determination Division which alone may refuse an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include on the notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellants are asked to provide the date on which notification of the decision was received, the claimant's social insurance number, the language in which they wish to be heard, and whether they wish to be heard in person; if represented, the name and address of representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pamphlet 'Appeal Procedure' advises appellants to be careful to include this information; it also stresses time limits and grounds to be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be heard and representation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations recognize the appellant's right to be heard (reg. 182(1),(2),(4)); practice is to never block access to the Board of a claimant who desires to be heard even if he initially forewent the right to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants are advised it is in their interest to attend or to delegate someone (e.g., union representative) and must provide representative details in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance in preparing appeals and impartiality of UIC staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The pamphlet urges appellants to contact UIC staff for assistance in preparing appeals; however, the UIC Manual forbids employees consulted for assistance from attempting to influence appellants regarding presentation of facts or the decision to file an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents may, under these constraints, inform appellants of outside agencies specializing in assistance to claimants. Appellants often distrust advice from the originator of the decision; outside help may increase withdrawal rates after re-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice as to ambiguous notice wording
rubrics_metrics.description: The wording of the notice of appeal may sometimes not clearly indicate that the claimant wishes to file an appeal; many claimants merely express their dissatisfaction without formal wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pamphlet and practice encourage careful notification; UIC accepts various expressions of intent and will not unduly block access where intent is present.
